learningObjective: Describe the MoE routing pipeline: gating, top-k expert selection, and token dispatch to experts.
stem: In a top-k MoE MLP layer with E experts, each token is routed to k experts based on a gating network. Which description of the dataflow is correct?

options.text: The gate produces scores over the E experts per token; top-k experts (typically k=2) are selected and each token contributes to those k experts' input batches with weights = softmax over the top-k scores. Only the k selected experts run their MLP on that token, and outputs are combined by the gate weights. Load balancing across experts is enforced by auxiliary losses / capacity limits.

The gating network selects a single expert per token; multi-expert (top-k > 1) MoE always requires k independent forward passes through the full MLP block, because token-to-expert routing is not amenable to batched execution.

The gate produces per-expert probabilities for each token; every token is routed to the expert with highest probability, and its output is scaled by that probability. The scaling is what preserves gradient flow through the routing decision.

Every token is sent to every expert; the gating scores are used only as a soft mask on the outputs so that experts with score 0 contribute nothing. The 'sparsity' of MoE is entirely about the sum of gating weights, not about avoided compute.

explanation: Top-k MoE (as in Switch Transformer, Mixtral) computes gating scores g = x @ W_gate of shape [B*N, E], selects the top-k experts per token, and normalizes the k selected scores (softmax over the k) to get combining weights. Each token is dispatched to k expert input batches; each expert runs a standard MLP over the tokens routed to it. Outputs from the k experts are combined by the normalized gate weights. Load balancing is a serious concern (some experts get too many tokens) and is addressed via auxiliary losses in training and capacity factors / dropping in serving.

optionExplanations.B: Wrong: k > 1 does not force k passes; a single grouped dispatch handles all k slots.
optionExplanations.C: Wrong: describes top-1 MoE only and mischaracterizes the scaling role.
optionExplanations.D: Wrong: sparsity means skipped compute; not every expert runs on every token.

assumptions: Discussion is of top-k sparse MoE at inference or training, not dense mixture.
Capacity limits and drop policies are implementation details not affecting the routing definition.
nonImplications: Does not imply MoE always improves throughput; imbalance and communication (in TP/EP) can hurt.
Does not imply that all-to-all is the only dispatch method; token-shuffle and grouped-GEMM approaches exist.

performanceClaim.scope: Top-k MoE routing and dispatch dataflow
